beats.title: Pre-init guard prevents a first-boot false positive
beats.note: Identical events on a dead-RTC boot (wallClock starts at 0). With the guard, BootCheck defers below MinPlausible and the first plausible NTP seeds cleanly. Without it, BootCheck seeds prevSample=0, so the first NTP looks like a huge forward jump and raises a false alert that only self-clears on the next sync.

beats.title: Honest forward jump: detected, blocks one NTP, then clears
beats.note: After a clean seed (floor=3), wallClock jumps forward to 9. The stale-floor check at BootCheck raises the alert (step 6). The first NTP still sees a jump vs prevSample so it stays raised (step 7); the next stable NTP clears it (step 9).

beats.title: Forward-poisoned floor stays raised across a reboot
beats.note: A Cadence write under a spoofed-high wallClock pushes the persisted floor to 11 and raises the alert (step 6). The poisoned floor survives the reboot (prevSample resets), and because the floor is still ahead of real time, the post-reboot NTP cannot clear it.

beats.title: Tolerance decides whether a moderate jump is an attack
beats.note: Same |7-3|=4 forward jump against floor=3. With Tol=2 it exceeds tolerance and raises; with Tol=5 it is within tolerance and stays quiet. Same spec, one constant flipped.
